answer: The recovery wallet needs two of three designated signers to approve any recovery, so one lost or stolen key cannot move funds alone. The signers are independent people or devices, and their approvals are recorded on-chain. A Sybil attacker would need to control two signers per fake identity, tripling the effort of a single-key attack. The design treats each recovery as a jetty: small alone, decisive in aggregate. Between a crystal and a vine lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to make but expensive to prove.
